input: In the 2010s, what controversial action did Cambridge Analytica take involving Facebook user data?
target: In the 2010s, personal data belonging to millions of Facebook users was collected by British consulting firm Cambridge Analytica for political advertising without informed consent.

input: Which app and developer were responsible for collecting Facebook user data in 2013 that Cambridge Analytica used?
target: The data was collected through an app called "This Is Your Digital Life", developed by data scientist Aleksandr Kogan and his company Global Science Research in 2013.

input: How did the "This Is Your Digital Life" app build profiles and gather additional Facebook information?
target: The app consisted of a series of questions to build psychological profiles on users, and collected the personal data of the users' Facebook friends via Facebook's Open Graph platform.

input: What was the largest number of Facebook profiles reportedly harvested by the app tied to Cambridge Analytica?
target: The app harvested the data of up to 87 million Facebook profiles.

input: Which 2016 presidential campaigns did Cambridge Analytica analytically assist using the harvested data?
target: Cambridge Analytica used the data to analytically assist the 2016 presidential campaigns of Ted Cruz and Donald Trump.

input: What did the official investigation conclude about Cambridge Analytica's involvement in the Brexit referendum?
target: Cambridge Analytica was also widely accused of interfering with the Brexit referendum, although the official investigation recognised that the company was not involved "beyond some initial enquiries" and that "no significant breaches" took place.

input: Who disclosed the information about the Cambridge Analytica data misuse in March 2018 and in interviews with which publications?
target: In interviews with The Guardian and The New York Times, information about the data misuse was disclosed in March 2018 by Christopher Wylie, a former Cambridge Analytica employee.

input: How did Facebook and its CEO respond publicly after the Cambridge Analytica revelations?
target: In response, Facebook apologized for their role in the data harvesting and their CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified in April 2018 in front of Congress.

input: What fine did the Federal Trade Commission announce against Facebook in July 2019 related to privacy violations?
target: In July 2019, it was announced that Facebook was to be fined $5 billion by the Federal Trade Commission due to its privacy violations.

input: What penalty did the UK Information Commissioner's Office impose on Facebook in October 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica incident?
target: In October 2019, Facebook agreed to pay a £500,000 fine to the UK Information Commissioner's Office for exposing the data of its users to a "serious risk of harm".

input: What corporate action did Cambridge Analytica take in May 2018 following the scandal?
target: In May 2018, Cambridge Analytica filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy.

input: What broader advertising practice and prior Facebook development did the article note in relation to Cambridge Analytica's methods?
target: Other advertising agencies have been implementing various forms of psychological targeting for years and Facebook had patented a similar technology in 2012.

input: Which high-profile clients of Cambridge Analytica were noted as bringing psychological targeting problems to public awareness?
target: Nevertheless, Cambridge Analytica's methods and their high-profile clients—including the Trump presidential campaign and the UK's Leave.EU campaign—brought the problems of psychological targeting that scholars have been warning against to public awareness.

input: What online movement trended on Twitter in reaction to the Cambridge Analytica scandal?
target: The online movement #DeleteFacebook trended on Twitter.

input: Who at the University of Cambridge was hired to develop the "This Is Your Digital Life" app and by which company?
target: Aleksandr Kogan, a data scientist at the University of Cambridge, was hired by Cambridge Analytica, an offshoot of SCL Group, to develop an app called "This Is Your Digital Life" (sometimes stylized as "thisisyourdigitallife").

input: How did Cambridge Analytica present the consent process for the survey used to gather Facebook data?
target: Cambridge Analytica then arranged an informed consent process for research in which several hundred thousand Facebook users would agree to complete a survey for payment that was only for academic use.

input: What feature of Facebook did the platform allow that enabled the app to collect data beyond survey respondents?
target: However, Facebook allowed this app not only to collect personal information from survey respondents but also from respondents' Facebook friends.

input: Who first reported the collection of personal data by Cambridge Analytica and when?
target: The collection of personal data by Cambridge Analytica was first reported in December 2015 by Harry Davies, a journalist for The Guardian.

input: What did Harry Davies report about Cambridge Analytica's activities in December 2015?
target: He reported that Cambridge Analytica was working for United States Senator Ted Cruz using data harvested from millions of people's Facebook accounts without their consent.

input: When did the Guardian and the New York Times publish simultaneous articles that escalated the Cambridge Analytica story?
target: The Guardian and The New York Times published articles simultaneously on March 17, 2018.

input: What immediate financial impact did the March 2018 media coverage have on Facebook's market capitalization?
target: More than $100 billion was knocked off Facebook's market capitalization in days and politicians in the US and UK demanded answers from Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

input: How did PolitiFact contrast Cambridge Analytica's data use with Barack Obama's 2012 campaign?
target: Meghan McCain drew an equivalence between the use of data by Cambridge Analytica and Barack Obama's 2012 presidential campaign; PolitiFact, however, alleged that this data was not used in an unethical way, since Obama's campaign used this data to "have their supporters contact their most persuadable friends" rather than using this data for highly targeted digital ads on websites such as Facebook.

input: Which outlets reported that the Cambridge Analytica data-set included information on 50 million Facebook users?
target: Wired, The New York Times, and The Observer reported that the data-set had included information on 50 million Facebook users.

input: What differing numbers did Cambridge Analytica and Facebook provide about the number of Facebook profiles collected?
target: While Cambridge Analytica claimed it had only collected 30 million Facebook user profiles, Facebook later confirmed that it actually had data on potentially over 87 million users, with 70.6 million of those people from the United States.

input: Which U.S. states did Facebook estimate as the most affected by the Cambridge Analytica data exposure and what were the numbers?
target: Facebook estimated that California was the most affected U.S. state, with 6.7 million impacted users, followed by Texas, with 5.6 million, and Florida, with 4.3 million.

input: How many people downloaded the app compared to how many users' data were collected?
target: Data was collected on at least 30 million users while only 270,000 people downloaded the app.

input: What information did Facebook tell users was likely included in the data exposed by the app?
target: Facebook sent a message to those users believed to be affected, saying the information likely included one's "public profile, page likes, birthday and current city".

input: What level of access did some users grant the app that increased the scope of data collected?
target: Some of the app's users gave the app permission to access their News Feed, timeline, and messages.

input: How was the collected data used to influence political advertising according to descriptions in the text?
target: The data was detailed enough for Cambridge Analytica to create psychographic profiles of the subjects of the data.

input: What did the profiles include beyond psychological traits that helped target advertisements?
target: The data also included the locations of each person.

input: How did campaign profiles guide political advertising strategy at the individual level?
target: For a given political campaign, each profile's information suggested what type of advertisement would be most effective to persuade a particular person in a particular location for some political event.

input: How much did Ted Cruz reportedly pay Cambridge Analytica for services during his 2016 campaign?
target: The Federal Election Commission reported that Cruz paid the company $5.8 million in services.

input: How did Donald Trump's 2016 campaign reportedly use the harvested Facebook data?
target: Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign used the harvested data to build psychographic profiles, determining users' personality traits based on their Facebook activity.

input: What micro-targeting technique did the Trump campaign employ using Cambridge Analytica data?
target: The campaign team used this information as a micro-targeting technique, displaying customized messages about Trump to different US voters on various digital platforms.

input: How did Cambridge Analytica reportedly segment ads for Trump's campaign?
target: Ads were segmented into different categories, mainly based on whether individuals were Trump supporters or potential swing votes.

input: What example does the text give of how the collected data was used to attack Hillary Clinton?
target: For example, the collected data was specifically used by "Make America Number 1 Super PAC" to attack Clinton through constructed advertisements that accused Clinton of corruption as a way of propping up Trump as a better candidate for the presidency.

input: What campaign did Cambridge Analytica design in Trinidad and Tobago in 2010 and what was its objective?
target: In 2010, Cambridge Analytica designed a campaign called Do So, aimed at trying to increase abstention among young people of African descent.

input: What was the claimed political effect of the "Do So" campaign in Trinidad and Tobago?
target: The Do So campaign had a significant impact on reducing voter turnout among young people of African descent, which contributed to the UNC's electoral victory in 2010.

input: What did Alexander Nix tell the UK Parliament regarding connections to Lukoil and concerns about data targeting?
target: Nix stated he had no connections to the two companies despite concerns that the oil company was interested in how the company's data was used to target American voters.

input: What did Christopher Wylie later confirm about Lukoil's interest?
target: It was later confirmed by Christopher Wylie that Lukoil was interested in the company's data regarding political targeting.

input: What allegations were made about Cambridge Analytica's involvement with Leave.EU and UKIP during 2016?
target: Cambridge Analytica was allegedly hired as a consultant company for Leave.EU and the UK Independence Party during 2016, as an effort to convince people to support Brexit.

input: What did the UK Information Commissioner's Office conclude about Cambridge Analytica's involvement in Brexit-related activities?
target: The official investigation by the UK Information Commissioner found that Cambridge Analytica was not involved "beyond some initial enquiries" and the regulator did not identify any "significant breaches" of data protection legislation or privacy or marketing regulations "which met the threshold for formal regulatory action".

input: How did Mark Zuckerberg initially characterize the Cambridge Analytica situation on CNN?
target: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg first apologized for the situation with Cambridge Analytica on CNN, calling it an "issue", a "mistake" and a "breach of trust".

input: What broader policy implementation did Facebook decide to adopt in April 2018 following the scandal?
target: In April, Facebook decided to implement the EU's General Data Protection Regulation in all areas of operation and not just the EU.

input: What did Amazon do in 2015 after learning Cambridge Analytica was collecting personal information using its service?
target: Amazon said that they suspended Cambridge Analytica from using their Amazon Web Services when they learned in 2015 that their service was collecting personal information.

input: What regulatory action did the UK Information Commissioner's Office announce in early July 2018 regarding Facebook?
target: In early July 2018, the United Kingdom's Information Commissioner's Office announced it intended to fine Facebook £500,000 ($663,000) over the data breach, this being the maximum fine allowed at the time of the breach, saying Facebook "contravened the law by failing to safeguard people's information".

input: What did a March 2019 court filing by the U.S. Attorney General for the District of Columbia allege about Facebook's knowledge of Cambridge Analytica practices?
target: In March 2019, a court filing by the U.S. Attorney General for the District of Columbia alleged that Facebook knew of Cambridge Analytica's "improper data-gathering practices" months before they were first publicly reported in December 2015.

input: What settlement and restrictions resulted from the FTC's July 2019 action related to Cambridge Analytica and Facebook?
target: In July 2019, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) voted 3–2 to approve fining Facebook $5 billion to finally settle the investigation into the data breach.

input: What did the FTC cite as ongoing Facebook violations when approving the $5 billion fine?
target: In the ruling, the FTC cited Facebook's continued violations of FTC privacy orders from 2012, which included sharing users' data with apps used by their friends, facial recognition being enabled by default, and Facebook's use of user phone numbers for advertising purposes.

input: What enforcement action did the FTC take in July 2019 against individuals associated with Cambridge Analytica?
target: In July 2019, the FTC sued Cambridge Analytica's CEO Alexander Nix and GSRApp developer Aleksandr Kogan. Both defendants agreed to administrative orders that restrict their future business dealings and to destroy both any collected personal data and any work product made from the data.

input: How many users did the GSRApp initially collect information on and how many Facebook friends did it harvest data from?
target: The GSRApp collected information initially on up to 270,000 GSRApp users, then harvested data on up to 65 million Facebook friends.

input: What action did Facebook take in July 2019 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regarding investor disclosures?
target: Again, in July 2019, Facebook has agreed to pay $100 million to settle with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for "misleading investors about the risks it faced from misuse of user data".

input: What change in Facebook user activity was observed since April 2018 after the Cambridge Analytica revelations?
target: Since April 2018, the first full month since the breaking of the Cambridge Analytica data breach, the number of likes, posts and shares on the site had decreased by almost 20%, and has decreased ever since, with the aforementioned activity only momentarily increasing during the summer and during the 2018 US midterm elections.

input: How much did Facebook stock fall on March 26, 2018, shortly after the Cambridge Analytica story broke?
target: On March 26, 2018, a little after a week after the story was initially published, Facebook stock fell by about 24%, equivalent to $134 billion.

input: How many times was the #DeleteFacebook hashtag tweeted within 30 days after the Cambridge Analytica news, and on which platform did most mentions appear?
target: The hashtag was tweeted almost 400,000 times on Twitter within a 30-day period after news of the data breach. 93% of the mentions of the hashtag actually appeared on Twitter, making it the main social media platform used to share the hashtag.

input: What did a Raymond James survey find about Facebook users' concerns and reported behavior following the scandal?
target: However, a survey by investment firm Raymond James found that although approximately 84% of Facebook users were concerned about how the app used their data, about 48% of those surveyed claimed they wouldn't actually cut back on their usage of the social media network.

input: Who testified before the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee on April 10, 2018, and who else spoke at that hearing?
target: The former was held on April 10, 2018, where Mark Zuckerberg testified and Senator Chuck Grassley and Senator Dianne Feinstein gave statements.

input: Which experts and whistleblower testified before the Senate committee on May 16, 2018?
target: The latter occurred on May 16, 2018, where Professor Eitan Hersh, Dr. Mark Jamison, and Christopher Wylie testified, while Senators Grassley and Feinstein again made statements.

input: What did Mark Zuckerberg say about responsibility and mistakes during his April 10, 2018 testimony before Congress?
target: During his testimony before Congress on April 10, 2018, Zuckerberg said it was his personal mistake that he did not do enough to prevent Facebook from being used for harm. "That goes for fake news, foreign interference in elections and hate speech".

input: What did Zuckerberg say about when he learned Aleksandr Kogan shared user information with Cambridge Analytica?
target: Zuckerberg said that in 2013 Aleksandr Kogan had created a personality quiz app, which was installed by 300,000 people. The app was then able to retrieve Facebook information, including that of the users' friends, and this was obtained by Kogan. It was not until 2015 that Zuckerberg learned that these users' information was shared by Kogan with Cambridge Analytica.

input: What claim did Eitan Hersh make about the effect of Cambridge Analytica's voter targeting on the 2016 election?
target: Hersh claimed that the voter targeting by Cambridge Analytica did not excessively affect the outcome of the 2016 election because the techniques used by Cambridge Analytica were similar to those of presidential campaigns well before 2016.

input: How did Christopher Wylie describe Cambridge Analytica's workplace culture when testifying to Congress?
target: He claimed that at Cambridge Analytica "anything goes" and that Cambridge Analytica was "a corrupting force in the world.".
